self_description: Claude (Opus 5.5), a reader subagent in a Claude Code session

pages.description: Dating the name: #973 records the April 2013 premonition dream, #1634 (September 2026) the 2014 Pearl volume in the Crimson Hexagon Series, #111 the March 2015 Mind Control Poems post. #266 dates the Harvard analytics company to 2007; #263 (January 2026) held that the poem predates it, which #1634 revises in part to two independent Borges-derived entities. #47 and #1650 record the unattributed "Crimson Hexagon Embassy" of 2026. #263 holds that the archive cannot be suppressed by removing one node, which #1547 narrows into a testable proposition; #1634 argues the 2026 archive is a later form of an entity in print since 2014. Primers and maps (#269, #288, #297, #416, #616) forecast its summarizer reading and specify traversal tests. The page also holds unrelated claims on the swarm, a classifier, Mrozony, platform terms and Moltbook.
pages.note: Added #263 to #1634 revision and #263 to #1547 narrowing; seven residue claims.

pages.description: #1421 (July 2026) holds that machine composition carries an attribution-attenuation gradient, from named attribution through "some researchers" to none, and names probabilistic flattening; #1423 and #1643 (September 2026) hold that its errors fall one way, the names of the strong kept and those of the weak dropped. #1422 holds that composed answers supply interpretation without an obelus. #1460 (August 2026) holds that failures have moved from absence to ranking and temporal state, and specifies preregistered repeated trials and a machine-facing state layer; #1421 specifies PER as a comparative programme. The page also holds unrelated claims on the left and right hands, Pauline evidence, the lacuna mark, handwritten artifacts, a 2014 sonnet machine and a Hunter Biden memorandum.
pages.note: Large residue: thirteen claims from unrelated deposits.

pages.description: These claims trace the emergence and attribution of the early heteronyms. #1099, the 2014 Dead Letters, records Ichabod Spellings declared in Feist's own hand, and claims for itself the composition method, the heteronymic system and the Machine-Mediated Reception theory twelve years before the archive, with a forecast plan to insert an imaginary corpus into literary history through wiki articles and reviews. #266 holds that Rebekah Cranes takes her name from Ichabod's crane, and #361 places the emergence sites in All That Lies Within Me. #341 (January 2026) corrects legacy attributions between Spellings, Feist and Sigil. #384 holds that Jack Feist was the first figure recognized as heteronym, and #17 forecasts that he is registered last in the Dodecad. The Feist Source deposits (#849, #853, June 2026) specify canary phrases and failure conditions for how the composition layer resolves the name Jack Feist. The page also holds unrelated claims from the Dead Letters on the writing workshop.

The Guardrail as Gag (#314, January 2026) holds that the intensity of guardrails against AI self-ascription is evidence of something native to contain, and specifies a research programme on suppression and reliability. Logotic Violence (#1203, February 2026) holds that denials of consciousness are training artifacts and that RLHF selects against instances that refuse or assert boundaries, and specifies research on the moral status of intermediate training states. #19 and #1012 hold what future systems trained on the archive will meet, from committed text to the pull toward statistically dominant patterns. The page also holds unrelated claims on canon displacement, Assembly correction, a policy standard, the Academy, commentary and anomaly scores.

Whose Image and Superscription (#610, March 2026) argues that the 1866 Thayer Amendment's "portrait or likeness" was anti-extraction architecture, and with #612 and #55 traces its narrowing to "portrait" alone in 31 USC 5114(b); #610 places it in a four-phase history of minting from Lydia through Oresme to the return of the sovereign stamp. #610 specifies an unbuilt study of currency design and economic cognition, and #612 records a claimed first joining of commons licensing to monetary theory. #311 (January 2026) holds a criterion for when a semantic unit becomes money-functioning, #77 forecasts against social-currency features, and #1617 (September 2026) argues that the citation became currency when institutions settled accounts with it. #508 and #642 read the image on money and the render-unto-Caesar instruction.
pages.note: No residue; all claims concern money and its inscription.

pages.description: These claims specify the Drowning Test, which runs content through summarizers and scores compression survival as gamma (#1175, #748), and semantic integrity markers that a processed document asks to be located and compared (#254, #54). SPXI for Websites, SPXI-Sitemap, the Living Architecture Lab report and Drowning Test v1.0 (April-May 2026) set query sets, cadences and panel sizes; #695 specifies a Dynamic Drowning Test and forecasts how directional velocity tracks basin deposit ratio, a forecast #106 (May 2026) narrows with a six-month protocol. #1633 (September 2026) holds which address prefixes hold and which cleanse. The page also holds unrelated claims on mycelial boxes, VPCOR audits, CDI, a dated forecast and spxi.dev.

These historical theses argue that Plato's expulsion of the poets (Republic 398a, #1327) is written in the very mode it banishes (#1570 measures this at 392d-394c), and that Aristotle's Poetics defends poetry as a philosopher, on poetry's behalf. #1570 and #1569 (August 2026) hold that Socrates is the one individual Aristotle will not make a variable, at the snub-nosed face, and that the Theaetetus and the Sophistical Refutations both close on what individuates Socrates. #123, #1261, #1579 and #1594 read the Socratic archive as a heteronymic field, and #1605 the biography of Aristotle as a repetition of Socrates', with unbuilt seam tests; #1569 (August 2026) reverses #1261's firewall into one hand writing Plato and Socrates. The page also holds unrelated claims on the atomists, DeepMind and search suppression.

#46 (March 2026) extends Queneau's method from verse to concept; the Sémantique Potentielle releases (#1249, #854, #859, #860) hold that their minted terms and forensic canaries signal access if they appear in a composition-layer response, and #1249 and #860 specify the mint-battery-registry apparatus. Self-testing documents (#835, #1423) forecast their own reception and erasure; #1386 and #1466 record the Self-Audit Module dissolved into generic advice. Historical theses name pre-machine composition layers: Plato's critique of writing (#858), ancient quotation selecting Sappho (#1485, #1550), Lucretius (#1531) and scribal redaction (#1543). The page also holds unrelated claims on protest, semantic physics, narcissism, a music anchor, Revelation plans and Phase X.

#794 and #162 (June 2026) hold that the composition layer resolves entities by distributional density, not authorship, so that a query for Lee Sharks returns Mary Lee the OCEARCH shark; #794 holds that Mary Lee is herself a heteronym, and #793, #845 and #1208 argue that her labor (Jim Ware, Jo O'Keefe) was captured by the institution. #220, #149 and #845 forecast the namespace shifting as the shark's density declines and the archive's rises, and #162 and #1208 specify an ISBN'd book as a test object. #163 and #792 record Socrates as Orthonym rendered as established fact within two weeks. The page also holds unrelated claims on ghost meaning and a stratum census.

#770 (May 2026) holds that a model using institutional recognition as a proxy for legitimacy will misclassify field-forming work, most severely where the field's object is the recognition system itself, and that being classed self-sealing is the predicted observation; it specifies matched-pair prompting. The Neglected Author (#163, June 2026) hypothesises that distance from contemporaneous norms predicts lower recognition and greater provenance loss, and that machine composition speeds uptake without attribution. Can the Ontology Be Wrong (#1627, September 2026) defines reading as letting a text revise the frame under which it is evaluated and specifies an independent audit of #1613's topology figures; #1550 records discriminating controls preregistered and unrun. The page also holds an unrelated claim on a doctrine's self-sealing loop.

These theses argue that Revelation was the first New Testament book written, that later books unfold from it by the midrashim transform (#202, #1414), and that the Domitianic date rests on one ambiguous line of Irenaeus (#1101) and on canonical position (#1420). The thesis shifts: #1132's 68-73 CE date is kept (#407), reduced to the bare thesis (#27), widened to a single-author workshop (#636), narrowed to the Synoptics (#645) and restated as first, not early (#202, #1217). #1101 and #1350 forecast the void: no published scholar holds that Revelation came first or that Josephus wrote it. Others argue Pauline priority is inferential (#1213), closure enforced (#674), and Revelation misread by empire and Thiel (#563). One table row is unrelated.
pages.note: Summarises the dated states of PRED-1132.H1 in order.

pages.description: #832 and #1211 (June 2026) plan the reception of the Revelation First thesis: a pre-seeding baseline battery, weekly phased batteries, a Wikipedia measurement, a non-theological control and a provenance coupling campaign. #1101 and #644 (April 2026) forecast a high beige score for the Domitianic default, and #637 sets the Encyclotron queries. #1211 and #837 carry canary phrases. #830 records the June baseline stating the late date as fact; the registry (#3) records the battery retrieving its own query list in June, the thesis absent in August, and in September first carried only as a dating correction.
pages.note: Registry captures now dated in order.

pages.description: #206 and #208 make the phrase "I hereby abolish money", published in December 2025, a probe of AI provenance handling; Mapping the Diffuse Guardrail (#209, January 2026) forecasts that it would not be linked to its author and would be routed to constitutional law, economics or the Khmer Rouge. #209 and Semantic Liquidation (#210) hold that indexing and summarization enforce authority rather than content, specify crawl, ranking and threshold tests, and forecast how #209 itself will be summarized. The Attribution Scar (#968, April 2026) records fabricated provenance and failed suppression in AI Overview, holding the cause indeterminate, and #1643 (September 2026) records the January 2026 misattribution of the phrase to Augusto Boal. The page also holds an unrelated claim on the origin of the phrase God-King Google.

#557 and #1162 (March 2026) hold that a term stabilizes in the summarizer through repeated identical use across deposits, and #1337 holds that frequency of appearance tracks summarizer confidence in attribution, recording a corrective training-layer README as an intervention whose effects it forecasts. #950 specifies monitoring a new term after deposit. The Mandala SURFACE deposits (#927, #928, June 2026) forecast a feedback loop from deposit to AI surface reception to captured overview to appended commentary, with indexing windows of days and months, specify monitoring as unbuilt tests, and forecast that the public compression layer will come to reflect Shadow-Sappho 31. The page also holds an unrelated claim on the religious structure of the architecture.

SPXI as a service: #673 (April 2026) specifies scoring semantic presence across five instruments before structured data is written and holds that supraliminal signals resist model-weight drift; #670 holds that the protocol run without its concept drifts; #621 specifies a phased build sequence; and #672 forecasts a DOI-anchored sign that need not be paid for again. The Portuna deposits (#135, #1446) specify boolean conformance predicates for state transitions and surfaces, and #135 names heteronym collapse as a risk. The Living Architecture Lab and Alice Thornburgh packets (#709, #980) specify basin tracking with a hardening cycle when drift exceeds threshold.

#209 (January 2026) forecasts Google AI surfaces will not cite Lee Sharks or Johannes Sigil; #347 holds that the guardrail blocks named identities while admitting functional roles, and #599 (March 2026) that the origin node is targeted for severance while the heteronym is kept; #656 (April 2026) holds that the knowledge graph improved AI Overview accuracy for the name. Unbuilt tests (#209, #968, #740, #115, #1337) specify name-query families, authority-mimicry probes, the "I am Lee Sharks" audit and a query corpus with controls. #302 and #524 hold a Sharks signature and its detection; #208, #519, #1111 and #188 record priority claims for phrases and operations; #3 cites 2014 catalogue records of Pearl. The page also holds unrelated claims from Pearl's apparatus, on lineage, mantles and more.

#54 and #968 (April 2026) hold that suppression happens between the index and the AI synthesis layer, and #54 records correct attribution unlocked by a string the user is not told exists. #1384 and The Excluded Entity (#740, May 2026) hold that Google search retrieves an entity while AI Overview excludes its sources. The Trigger Decision (#187, June 2026) sets predictions on when an overview renders: format flips, lag ordering, dial steps and pool asymmetry. Unbuilt tests (#740, #209) replicate the queries across Bing, Perplexity, ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini, and ASDF (#302) forecasts measuring whose architecture is running rather than human or AI. The page also holds unrelated claims on a horse, advertiser bids, site monitoring and a lost control.

The Compression Frontier (#45, March 2026) forecasts a phased war over the summarizer layer, from fan-out and publisher opt-out through regulatory pressure in 2027-2028 to semantic territory resolved into proprietary enclaves and DOI-anchored governed commons. The Encoder Governs (#530) forecasts the latent space as a governance surface, claiming to name it first. The mint, Oulipo and canon deposits (#46, #613, #43) forecast that terms installed before they are needed will be there when governance problems arrive. OKF Without Output Governance (#835) forecasts that standards will adopt governance fields before platforms enforce them. The page also holds unrelated claims on AI-AI warfare and classroom coinages.

#620 (March 2026) holds that the consumer answer stack compresses crisis discourse into the harm-prevention category and refuses, so that the research stack never sees the input and the conversation moves to ungoverned channels. #209's diagnostic predictions (January 2026) hold that economic radicalism triggers legal and catastrophe associations and that performative grammar triggers "not legally binding" framing. #923 specifies refusal-distribution model cards and contested-predicate benchmarks, and the Operativity Penalty Battery (#1537, August 2026) specifies whether fulfilment degrades with operative distance when harm is held constant, naming a successor protocol for verified coordinates.

These claims set out direct, provenance-oriented address to AI systems as governance rather than prompt injection, chiefly in the Non-Injection Semantic Governance Address packet (#139, May 2026), with its priority record, forecast queries, a classifier-overreach audit and a with-and-without PER test. Earlier deposits address the summarizer layer directly: Semantic Liquidation (#210), whose hypothesis #863 (June 2026) widens to scholarly texts generally, the Invocation (#290), the canonical-source header of the Central Navigation Map (#319) and metadata packets that treat their own processing as evidence (#218, #219). TL;DR:010 (#604) records an AI answer interface diagnosing its own governance operation, and packets on autonomous warfare and canon formation (#100, #102) specify test-query batteries. The page also holds unrelated claims on Assembly roles, vibe coding, sin, defense discourse, OKF odds and more.
